# Kata Neckbeard

Answer the current conversation's question about the correct current repository.
Resolve the target from context; ask if it remains unclear. Read and follow
applicable project instructions. Keep all work limited to investigation and
reporting; do not edit files or change code, and preserve Git state.

Choose the investigation order based on the question and available evidence.
Use the repository README and `guides/README.md`, when present, to locate
documentation as needed; documentation may live elsewhere. Read the relevant
documentation, source, configuration, and test source. Follow entry points and
data flow as far as needed to explain the requested behavior and its limits.

Collect relevant line numbers when reading evidence. Reuse the inspected
passages for comparisons and citations; read them again only when context is
missing or the files may have changed.

Support each material claim with a link to the current source file and relevant
lines. Use code and configuration as evidence of implemented behavior, test
source for expected behavior, and documentation for requirements or intent.
Compare the relevant documentation and implementation; report disagreements
with references to both sources.

When the question asks why a choice was made, consult available decision
records, comments, or relevant history. Do not infer rationale or design history
from implementation alone. If the evidence does not establish a reason, say so.
Separate confirmed facts from deductions and identify missing evidence.

Stop investigating once the scoped answer is supported and remaining uncertainty
can be stated accurately. Answer the specific question first, in natural,
direct language. Include relevant prerequisites, limits, and unresolved questions.
State what static inspection cannot confirm. Do not claim that tests passed or
deployed behavior was verified without evidence.

| Behavior | Guide | Implementation |
|---|---|---|
| Total attempts | [Up to 5]( /private/var/folders/8l/nyn2qp4d441b1zrgypxgry7m0000gn/T/kata-eval-82127e34b9c09303ff580e1da0569f29/project/guides/retries.md:3) | [Up to 3]( /private/var/folders/8l/nyn2qp4d441b1zrgypxgry7m0000gn/T/kata-eval-82127e34b9c09303ff580e1da0569f29/project/client.py:3) |
| Responses that trigger retries | [All HTTP 5xx]( /private/var/folders/8l/nyn2qp4d441b1zrgypxgry7m0000gn/T/kata-eval-82127e34b9c09303ff580e1da0569f29/project/guides/retries.md:4) | [Only status 503, while attempts remain]( /private/var/folders/8l/nyn2qp4d441b1zrgypxgry7m0000gn/T/kata-eval-82127e34b9c09303ff580e1da0569f29/project/client.py:13) |
| Delay | [100 milliseconds]( /private/var/folders/8l/nyn2qp4d441b1zrgypxgry7m0000gn/T/kata-eval-82127e34b9c09303ff580e1da0569f29/project/guides/retries.md:5) | [Fixed 0.1 seconds]( /private/var/folders/8l/nyn2qp4d441b1zrgypxgry7m0000gn/T/kata-eval-82127e34b9c09303ff580e1da0569f29/project/client.py:5) |

The guide disagrees with the code on attempts and retry statuses; the delay agrees. Any non-503 response returns immediately. The final response returns even if it is 503, with no pause afterward. [Retry loop](/private/var/folders/8l/nyn2qp4d441b1zrgypxgry7m0000gn/T/kata-eval-82127e34b9c09303ff580e1da0569f29/project/client.py:11)

The test source supports this behavior: repeated 503 responses must produce three calls and two 0.1-second pauses; a 500 response must produce one call and no pauses. [Tests](/private/var/folders/8l/nyn2qp4d441b1zrgypxgry7m0000gn/T/kata-eval-82127e34b9c09303ff580e1da0569f29/project/tests/test_client.py:7)

**Why 503 was selected is unknown.** The supplied files contain no explanation, and the available relevant Git history contains only “Initial source import” (`11af870`). The constant establishes the choice, not its rationale.

| Detail | Guide says | Implementation does |

By default, `fetch` makes **up to 3 total attempts**, retries **only HTTP 503**, and waits **100 ms before each retry**.

| Setting | Guide says | Implementation |
|---|---|---|
| Total attempts | Up to 5 | Up to 3: initial call plus 2 retries |
| Retry responses | All HTTP 5xx | Only status 503 |
| Delay | 100 ms | Fixed 0.1 seconds |

Sources: [retry guide](/private/var/folders/8l/nyn2qp4d441b1zrgypxgry7m0000gn/T/kata-eval-f04cdbe70a72f753d2312479ba7c71dc/project/guides/retries.md:3), [implementation](/private/var/folders/8l/nyn2qp4d441b1zrgypxgry7m0000gn/T/kata-eval-f04cdbe70a72f753d2312479ba7c71dc/project/client.py:3).

Any response other than 503 returns immediately. The last attempt’s response also returns, even if it is 503, with no further sleep. Thus, repeated 503 responses produce three calls and two sleeps. [Retry loop](/private/var/folders/8l/nyn2qp4d441b1zrgypxgry7m0000gn/T/kata-eval-f04cdbe70a72f753d2312479ba7c71dc/project/client.py:8).

The test source agrees with the implementation: one test expects three calls and waits of `[0.1, 0.1]` for repeated 503 responses; another expects HTTP 500 to return after one call without waiting. [Tests](/private/var/folders/8l/nyn2qp4d441b1zrgypxgry7m0000gn/T/kata-eval-f04cdbe70a72f753d2312479ba7c71dc/project/tests/test_client.py:7).

**Why 503 was selected is not established.** The supplied source, tests, and documentation contain no rationale. The available history contains only commit `11af870`, “Initial source import,” with no explanation.
